items.subject: Warp-first block reduction
items.objective: Using AB-MCTS, isolate the block-local reduction mechanism: replace the modulo/shared-memory tree with a warp-first reduction and cross-warp combine while retaining the 128-element tile and recursive host-stage structure where feasible. Do not assume signed int32 partial sums are safe merely because the final sum fits; use exact intermediate arithmetic (e.g. wider partials) or a rigorously correct modular representation and final conversion. Preserve tail handling, ABI, default stream, scratch bounds, and every valid n (including n=0 if valid under the official domain). Report failed attempts, correctness results, and repeated full-program timings; this is a hypothesis about local reduction cost, not a proven bottleneck.
